extracted.intended_audience: readers and users of Terence Tao's Analysis I (students, instructors, copyeditors, LaTeX authors, errata contributors)
extracted.subtask_short: Analysis I errata and LaTeX style
extracted.subtask_description: Errata, editorial guidance, and LaTeX/notation style recommendations for producing, typesetting, and using Terence Tao's textbook Analysis I (fourth edition). Includes suggested content reorderings, notation consistency, and comment-formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon spacing in maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Colons in maps should be spaced using the \colon LaTeX macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \colon rather than a plain colon character when typesetting maps/functions so spacing is consistent (e.g., use f\colon A \to B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \text, not \hbox, for subscripted text
rubrics_metrics.description: For subscripted textual material use \text rather than \hbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid \hbox in subscripts; prefer \text{...} (from amsmath/textcomp) for correct font and spacing in math-mode subscripts/ superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper math-mode for numbers and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers and certain symbols must be placed in math mode (e.g., the digit 0 should be in math mode where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numerals and math symbols appear in $...$ or \( ... \) as appropriate; this fixes placement and font issues cited (e.g., 'Some numbers (such as 0) are not properly placed in math mode in certain places').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate LaTeX macros for ellipses and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \dots instead of \ldots for ellipses in most contexts; use \limsup and \liminf instead of \lim \sup and \lim \inf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace occurrences of \ldots with \dots where appropriate, and use the single-command macros \limsup and \liminf for proper spacing and typesetting. The page lists these as general LaTeX issues to fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent definition notation (use :=)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions should use := rather than = when introducing new notation/definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the text currently uses = to define a new object, change to := for clarity (several errata note replacing = with := in definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'iff' for biconditional/definition statements
rubrics_metrics.description: In definitions/statements that require equivalence, use 'iff' (if and only if) rather than a plain 'if'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace isolated 'if' in definition statements with 'iff' (e.g., change 'if' to 'iff' in Definition 3.1.14 and similar places) to remove ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation consistency across chapters and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistent notation across the book (e.g., consistent use of symbols, names, and codomain/codomain wording).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: change 'what its range is' to 'what its codomain is' in Example 3.3.21; ensure repeated symbols/notations match between related exercises and definitions; harmonize occurrences of symbols across chapters (many 'Page ???' items point out inconsistent notation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specificity for cross-volume citations
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to material in the companion volume, explicitly indicate 'of Analysis II' (or the relevant volume/section) rather than just a section number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous errata request changing references like 'Section 1.2' to 'Section 1.7 of Analysis II' or explicitly append 'of Analysis II' to avoid ambiguity between volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical ordering and placement of propositions/exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange propositions, proofs, and exercises in an order that improves logical flow and pedagogical progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The errata recommend moving specific propositions/exercises (e.g., Proposition 9.4.13 before Proposition 9.4.10, move Exercise 7.3.3 to Section 7.2, permute parts of Proposition 8.2.6) so that prerequisites are presented before dependent material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove redundant or duplicated material
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete redundant text/exercises and avoid duplicated introductions or repeated material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: delete the second part of Exercise 3.4.6 as redundant; remove duplicated introductions of symbols in proofs; delete paragraphs that are essentially replicated elsewhere (noted in several errata).

rubrics_metrics.name: Add missing exercises or clarify exercise statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Add exercises where pedagogically useful and clarify exercise prompts to be precise and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: add an exercise to Section 4.1 suggested in the errata; add an exercise regarding Darboux-type results; modify Exercise statements to include missing hypotheses or conventions (e.g., add 'If' in Exercise 5.4.9(ii), add conditions to geometric series formula in Exercise 7.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical correctness of statements and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct mathematical errors in statements, hypotheses, or proofs (e.g., incorrect references to lemmas/theorems, incorrect quantifiers, mis-stated conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errata examples: change 'transfinite induction' to 'Zorn's lemma' in a reference; relax or correct hypothesis values (e.g., relax condition q > 1 where appropriate); correct lemma/theorem references and fix missing qualifiers in statements and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar, punctuation, and prose clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix grammatical, punctuation, capitalization, and wording issues to improve readability and correctness of prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many small errata are of this type: missing spaces ('ontheir' -> 'on their'), incorrect capitalisation ('without' -> 'Without'), wrong word choice ('one obvious guess' -> 'One obvious guess'), fixing stray extra words, and punctuation adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical fixes in displays and parenthetical remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure mathematical displays and parentheticals are correctly typeset (matching parentheses, correct placement of absolute values, colons/semicolons, removed stray characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in errata: close missing parentheses, remove stray characters appearing before symbols in displays, adjust delimiters in displays for consistency (remove extra absolute values, enlarge parentheses etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and naming conventions (use of 'roles' vs 'rôles', 'codomain' vs 'range')
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer contemporary, unambiguous terminology and correct diacritics/word forms accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace obsolete spellings or diacritics when not needed (e.g., 'rôles' -> 'roles') and standardize mathematical terminology (e.g., 'codomain' vs 'range' as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions for extended reals and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend definitions to cover extended real number values where context requires (e.g., supremum/infimum for sequences taking extended-real values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errata suggest explicitly extending the notion of supremum/infimum to sequences that take values in the extended reals, not just the reals (Definition 6.4.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions about the axiom of choice and forward references
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making claims or exercises that require axioms not yet introduced; adjust or relocate such material so prerequisites are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: delete the last sentence of Exercise 4.4.3 since the axiom of choice is not yet introduced; reorder or rephrase statements that presuppose later material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction for commenters: how to enter LaTeX in blog comments
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter LaTeX in comments on the blog, wrap code with $latex ...$ and double backslashes for backslashes in the content. Avoid angle brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment authors should use $latex <Your LaTeX code>$ (without angle brackets) and double backslashes \\ for backslashes. The page points to the about page for additional commenting policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index and cross-volume page-number clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify index entries when the same index is used across multiple volumes so page numbers indicate which volume is referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errata note that the index is duplicated across vols. 1 & 2 but page numbers do not indicate which volume — add conventions or qualifiers to index entries to remove ambiguity.
